items.comment: Accurate and matches the code (no @specialized annotations are claimed, correctly unlike AbstractFunction1). Minor wording redundancy: 'Extending this class allows a function value to be defined by extending a class rather than the trait' repeats 'extending' twice in one sentence. Sibling file AbstractFunction1.scala phrases the same idea in one combined sentence without the repetition ('A base class for one-parameter function implementations, allowing a function value to be defined by extending a class rather than the [[scala.Function1]] trait.'); splitting AbstractFunction20's version into two sentences with the doubled 'extending' is not wrong but reads slightly clunkier and is stylistically inconsistent with the established family phrasing.

Wording matches the established convention used in scala.Function20 ('the type of the Nth argument'); R's description ('the return type of this function') is a harmless minor variant of Function20's 'the result type of the function', not an inaccuracy.
